sections.english: This too is a counter to pretension, that you have lost now the chance to live your whole life, or at least your adult life, as a philosopher: indeed it has become clear to many, yourself included, that you are far from philosophy. You are tarnished, then: difficult for you now to win the reputation of a philosopher, and your own station in life is an opposing factor. But if you have truly seen where the truth lies, then drop all other concerns and simply ensure that the rest of your life, whatever length the gods grant, is lived as your nature demands.
sections.chinese: 此亦是抗拒虚矫之一法——你如今已失去以哲人身份度过整个一生、或至少成年之一生的机会：事实上，在许多人和你自己看来，你离哲学已远。你已被玷染：如今要赢得哲人之名对你而言是困难的，而你自身在世间的处境亦是一种阻碍。然而，若你已真正看清真理之所在，那便放下其他一切顾虑，只须确保余下之人生——无论诸神所赐予者何其短长——皆依照你之本性所需而度过。

sections.english: Ask yourself this about each action: 'How does this sit with me? Shall I regret it?' In a short while I am dead and all things are gone. What more do I want, if this present work is that of an intelligent and social being, sharing one law with god?
sections.chinese: 对每一行动，以此自问：「此事合我心意否？我会追悔否？」须臾之间我便将死去，一切皆逝。若此当下之作为，乃是一智性而社会性之存在者，与神共享同一法则——那我更有何求？

sections.english: Alexander, Julius Caesar, Pompey — what are they to Diogenes, Heraclitus, Socrates? These men saw into reality, its causes and its material, and their directing minds were their own masters. As for the former, they were slaves to all their ambitions.
sections.chinese: 亚历山大、尤利乌斯·凯撒、庞培——比起第欧根尼、赫拉克利特、苏格拉底，这些算得什么？后者洞见实在、其原因与物质，其主导之心灵乃自我主宰。至于前者，他们不过是己之诸般野心的奴隶。

sections.english: Even if you burst with indignation, they will still carry on regardless.
sections.chinese: 纵使你气得炸开，他们照样我行我素。

sections.english: First, do not be upset: all things follow the nature of the Whole, and in a little while you will be no one and nowhere, as is true now even of Hadrian and Augustus. Next, concentrate on the matter in hand and see it for what it is. Remind yourself of your duty to be a good man and rehearse what man's nature demands: then do it straight and unswerving, or speak as you think best, as long as you do it without affectation.
sections.chinese: 首先，不要烦乱：万物皆遵循宇宙整体之本性，而稍过片刻，你便将寂寂无名、无处可觅——正如哈德良与奥古斯都如今亦是如此。其次，专注于手头之事，看清其本来面目。提醒自己要做一个好人，并温习人之本性所要求者：然后径直去做，不偏不倚，或如你所思为佳者去言说——只要你在做时毫无造作之态。

sections.english: The work of universal nature is to translate this reality to another, to change things, to take them from here and carry them there. All things are mutations, but there is equality too in their distribution. All is familiar: no cause then for fear of anything new.
sections.chinese: 宇宙本性之工作，即是将此一实在转化为另一实在，改变事物，将物从此处取而运至彼处。一切皆是在变易之中，然而变化之分派亦是平等的。一切皆是熟悉之旧事：故无由惧怕任何新物。

sections.english: Every living organism is fulfilled when it follows the right path for its own nature. For a rational nature the right path is to withhold assent to anything false or obscure in the impressions made on its mind, to direct its impulses solely to social action, to reserve its desires and aversions to what is in our power, and to welcome all that is assigned by universal nature.
sections.chinese: 每一活之有机体，当其遵循适宜其本性之正路时，便得了成全。对于理性本性，正路乃是：不赞同其心灵所接获印象中任何虚假或隐晦之物；将冲动纯粹导向社会性之行动；将其欲望与厌恶限定于吾辈权能之内；并接纳宇宙本性所分配之一切。

sections.english: Not possible to study. But possible to rein in arrogance; possible to triumph over pleasures and pains; possible to rise above mere glory; possible not to be angry with the unfeeling and the ungrateful, and even, yes, to care for them.
sections.chinese: 未必能够研读。但可以克制傲慢；可以战胜逸乐与痛苦；可以超乎虚浮之荣名；可以不恼怒于那些麻木与忘恩负义之人——甚至，是的，仍去关心他们。

sections.english: Let nobody any more hear you blaming palace life: don't hear yourself blaming it.
sections.chinese: 别让任何人再听见你抱怨宫廷生活：也别让自己听见你抱怨它。

sections.english: Regret is a censure of yourself for missing something beneficial. The good must be something beneficial, and of concern to the wholly good person. No wholly good person would regret missing a pleasure. Therefore pleasure is neither beneficial nor a good.
sections.chinese: 后悔乃是因错失了某有益之物而对己之责备。善者必为有益之物，且为全然之善人所关切者。无一全然之善人会后悔错过一桩逸乐。故逸乐既非有益，亦非善好。

sections.english: What is this thing in itself, in its own constitution? What are its elements of substance and material, and of cause? What is its function in the world? What is its duration?
sections.chinese: 此物在其自身构造中究是什么？其实体与物质，以及其原因的元素是什么？它在世间之功能为何？其存续之时间又几何？

sections.english: When you are reluctant to get up from your sleep, remind yourself that it is your constitution and man's nature to perform social acts, whereas sleep is something you share with dumb animals. Now what accords with the nature of each being is thereby the more closely related to it, the more in its essence, and indeed the more agreeable.
sections.chinese: 当你不愿从睡乡起身时，提醒自己：履行社会性之行动是你之构造与人之本性，而睡眠则是你与哑畜所共有的。凡契合于每类存在者之本性者，便因此更为亲于该类存在者，更在其本质中，且也更令人满足愉快。

sections.english: Constantly test your mental impressions — each one individually, if you can: investigate the cause, identify the emotion, apply the analysis of logic.
sections.chinese: 恒常检验你心灵之印象——若能，便逐一而试：探究其原因，识别其所涉之情，运用逻辑之分析。

sections.english: Whenever you meet someone, ask yourself first this immediate question: 'What beliefs does this person hold about the good and bad in life?' Because if he believes this or that about pleasure and pain and their constituents, about fame and obscurity, death and life, then I shall not find it surprising or strange if he acts in this or that way: and I shall remember that he is forced to act so.
sections.chinese: 每遇见一人，先以此当下之问自问：「此人于人生中之善与恶持有何种信念？」因为若他对逸乐与痛苦及其诸组成、对名声与默默无闻、对生与死抱持这般这般之信念，那么他这般这般行事，我便不以为异、不以为怪了：并且我当记得，他乃是不得不如此行事。

sections.english: It would be absurd to be surprised at a fig-tree bearing figs. Remember that there is as little cause for surprise if the world brings forth fruits such as these when the crop is there. Equally absurd for a doctor or ship's captain to be surprised at fever in a patient or a head-wind springing up.
sections.chinese: 无花果树结无花果，若因此惊异，便是荒谬。当记得：若世界在庄稼成熟时节产生如此之果实，亦同样不足为惊。医生若对病人发烧感到意外，或船长对逆风骤起感到吃惊，也同样的荒谬。

sections.english: Remember that to change course or accept correction leaves you just as free as you were. The action is your own, driven by your own impulse and judgement, indeed your own intelligence.
sections.chinese: 切记：更改方向，或接受纠正，并不减少你之自由。行动仍是你自己的，为你自己之冲动与判断所驱使——甚至，就是你自身之智识。

sections.english: If the choice is yours, why do the thing? But if it is another's choice, what do you blame — atoms or gods? Either is madness. There is no blame. If you can, put him right: if you can't, at the least put the matter itself right. If that too is impossible, what further purpose does blame serve? Nothing should be done without purpose.
sections.chinese: 若选择在你，为何要做那事？但若选择在别人，你责怪谁——原子，还是诸神？两者皆疯狂。其实并无责怪。若你能够，纠正他：若你不能，至少把事本身纠正。若这也行不通，责怪又有何意义？无事当无目的地施行。

sections.english: What dies does not pass out of the universe. If it remains here and is changed, then here too it is resolved into the everlasting constituents, which are the elements of the universe and of you yourself. These too change, and make no complaint of it.
sections.chinese: 死亡之物并不逸出宇宙。若它留在此间而变化，则也在此间消解为永恒之构成元素——这些元素既属宇宙，亦属你自己。此等元素亦变化，并不抱怨。

sections.english: Everything has come into being for a purpose — a horse, say, a vine. Does this surprise you? Even the sun will say, 'I came into being for a purpose': likewise the other gods. For what purpose, then, were you created? For your pleasure? Just see whether this idea can be entertained.
sections.chinese: 一切皆具一目的而生成——譬如一匹马、一株藤蔓。这让你惊讶吗？连太阳也会说：「我因一目的而存在」：其余诸神亦然。那么，你又是因何目的而被造？为了你的逸乐？且看此念能否被认真对待。

sections.english: Nature's aim for everything includes its cessation just as much as its beginning and its duration — like someone throwing up a ball. How can it be good for the ball on the way up and bad on the way down, or even when it hits the ground? How can it be good for a bubble when it forms, and bad when it bursts? The same for a lamp too.
sections.chinese: 自然为每物所设定之目标，既囊括其终止，正如囊括其起始与延续——如同一个人向上抛球。球在上升之时如何为善好、在下落之时又如何为坏，甚至落于地上时为坏？一气泡形成时如何为好、破灭时又如何为坏？灯烛亦然。

sections.english: Turn it inside out and see what it is like, what it becomes in age, sickness, death. Life is short both for praiser and praised, for the remembering and the remembered. And this, moreover, in just a cranny of one continent: even here not all are attuned to each other, or even an individual to himself. Yet the whole earth is just a point.
sections.chinese: 将物翻转过来，看透它本质如何，在年迈、疾病、死亡之中它又变得怎样。寿命之短促，不论于赞扬者或被赞扬者、于记忆者与被记忆者，皆是一般无二。况且，这一切不过发生在一块大陆之一罅隙中：即便在此处，也并非人人彼此协调——甚或个人与自己也不协调。然而整个地球，不过是宇宙中一粒微点。

sections.english: Concentrate on the subject or the act in question, on principle or meaning. You deserve what you're going through. You would rather become good tomorrow than be good today.
sections.chinese: 专注于事物本身，或所问之行动，或所涉之原则或含义。你正在经历的，正是你应得的。你宁愿明日成善，而不愿今日即是善人。

sections.english: Doing something? I do it with reference to the benefit of mankind. Something happening to me? I accept it in reference to the gods and the universal source from which all things spring interrelated.
sections.chinese: 在做什么事？我做它以涉及人类之福祉。有事临到我身？我接纳它以涉及诸神，及那万物彼此牵联所自流出之宇宙源头。

sections.english: Just as you see your bath — all soap, sweat, grime, greasy water, the whole thing disgusting — so is every part of life and every object in it.
sections.chinese: 正如你看见你的浴场——满是肥皂沫、汗渍、污垢、油腻浊水，整件事令人作呕——生命之每一部分及其中之每一对象，亦皆如此。

sections.english: Lucilla buried Verus, then Lucilla was buried. Secunda buried Maximus, then Secunda next. So with Epitynchanus and Diotimus, Antoninus and Faustina. The same story always. Celer saw Hadrian to his grave, then went to his own grave. Where are they now, those sharp minds, those prophets or prigs? Certainly all ephemeral. All dead long ago.
sections.chinese: 卢西拉葬了维鲁斯，而后卢西拉亦被人葬。塞昆达葬了马克西穆斯，而后塞昆达随之而去。埃皮廷卡努斯与狄奥提穆斯、安东尼努斯与福斯蒂娜——莫不如此。同样之故事，反复重演。凯勒送哈德良入葬，而后也入了自己之葬。那些敏锐之心思、那些先知或自诩不凡之徒——如今安在？无非皆朝生暮死。一切皆早已故去。

sections.english: Man's joy is to do man's proper work. And work proper to man is benevolence to his own kind, disdain for the stirrings of the senses, diagnosis of the impressions he can trust, contemplation of universal nature and all things thereby entailed.
sections.chinese: 人之乐，在于行人之恰当事务。而人之恰当事务，乃是：善待同类，鄙弃感官之扰动，辨识他可信任之印象，沉思宇宙本性及由此而涉之一切。

sections.english: Three relations. First, to your environment; second, to the divine cause which is the source of all that happens to all men; third, to your fellows and contemporaries.
sections.chinese: 三种关系。其一，与你之周遭环境；其二，与那作为一切人事源泉之神性原因；其三，与你的同侪及同时之人。

sections.english: Pain is an evil either to the body — so let the body give its evidence — or to the soul. But the soul can preserve its own clear sky and calm voyage by not assessing pain as an evil. Every judgement, every impulse, desire and rejection is within the soul, where nothing evil can penetrate.
sections.chinese: 痛苦对身体而言或是恶——那便让身体就此作其证言——或对灵魂也如是。但灵魂可以保持自身清朗之天空与沉稳之航程，只要它不评断痛苦为恶。每一判断、每一冲动、每一欲望与拒绝，皆发生于灵魂之内——而在此处，无一恶物得以渗入。

sections.english: Erase the impressions on your mind by constantly saying to yourself: 'It is in my power now to keep this soul of mine free from any vice or passion, or any other disturbance at all: but seeing all things for what they are, I can treat them on their merits.' Remember this power which nature gives you.
sections.chinese: 抹去你心灵上之印象，恒常自谓：「我此刻有能力使此灵魂不受任何恶行或激情、或任何其他侵扰之染：看清万物之本来面目，我便可依其应得之对待而处理之。」记取自然赋予你的此一能力。

sections.english: When you speak in the senate or to any individual, be straightforward, not pedantic. Use language which rings true.
sections.chinese: 在元老院中发言，或任对某个人说话，当直截而不学究。用那听来真切的言辞。

sections.english: The court of Augustus — wife, daughter, grandsons, step-sons, sister, Agrippa, relatives, household, friends, Areius, Maecenas, doctors, diviners: an entire court dead. Go on now to other cases, where it is not the death of just one individual but of a whole family, like the Pompeys. And there is the famous inscription on the tomb: 'Last of his line'. Think of all the anxiety of previous generations to produce a successor: and then, necessarily, someone is the last. Here again the death of a whole line.
sections.chinese: 奥古斯都之宫廷——妻子、女儿、诸孙、诸继子、姊妹、阿格里帕、诸亲族、家众、友朋、阿瑞乌斯、梅塞纳斯、医者、占卜师：整座宫廷皆已死去。再看其他案例——非仅一人之死，而是整族之家，如庞培一族。而墓碑上那著名的铭文写着：「此族最后一人」。想想前代之人何等焦虑地求嗣以延宗续祀：而必然地，某人终成最后一人。此处又是一整族血脉之泯灭。

sections.english: You must compose your life action by action, and be satisfied if each action achieves its own end as best can be: and no one can prevent you from that achievement. 'But there will be some external obstacle.' No obstacle, though, to justice, self-control, and reason. 'But perhaps some other source of action will be obstructed.' Still, by willing acceptance of the obstacle and by a calm change over to what is allowed, another action will immediately take its place which fits the composition we are talking of.
sections.chinese: 你必须一行接一行地缀成你之生命，若每一行动尽其可能达成了它自身之目的，便当满足：且无人能阻你达成此点。「但会有些外在之障碍。」然而，对正义、自制与理性，没有障碍。「但也许行动之某些其他方面将受阻。」即便如此，藉由乐意接纳障碍，并平心静气地转到较可为之他事，另一行动便将立时取而代之，正合我们所说之生命缀构。

sections.english: Accept humbly: let go easily.
sections.chinese: 谦卑地领受，轻易地放手。

sections.english: If you have ever seen a severed hand or foot, or a head cut off and lying some way away from the rest of the body — analogous is what someone does to himself, as far as he can, when he will not accept his lot and severs himself from society or does some unsocial act.
sections.chinese: 你若曾见过一只切断之手或足，或一颗被砍下且远远脱离身体其余部分的头颅——类比于此，便是一个人尽其力所能地对自己所做的：不接受自己之遭际，将自己与社会分割开来，或行某种反社会之举动。

sections.english: Just as the nature of the Whole is the source of all other faculties in every rational creature, so it has given us this power too. In the same way that nature turns to its own purpose anything obstructive or contrary, placing it in the fated scheme of things and making it part of itself, so the rational being can turn any obstacle into material for himself and use it for whatever purpose he has set.
sections.chinese: 正如宇宙整体之自然是每一理性造物中一切官能之来源，它也将此一能力赐给了我们。自然将任何障碍或相逆之物转用来为其自身之目的，纳入注定的事物格局中，使之成为自身之一部分——同样地，理性存在者也可将任何障碍转为己用之材料，并将其用于自己所设定之任何目的。

sections.english: Do not let the panorama of your life oppress you, do not dwell on all the various troubles which may have occurred in the past or may occur in the future. Just ask yourself in each instance of the present: 'What is there in this work which I cannot endure or support?' You will be ashamed to make any such confession. Then remind yourself that it is not the future or the past that weighs on you, but always the present, and the present becomes lighter when you isolate it and take your mind to task.
sections.chinese: 勿让你生命之全幅景象压迫于你，勿沉湎于过去已发生或将来可能发生之种种烦恼。只需在每一当下之情形中自问：「此事之中，有何为我所不可忍、不可堪者？」你必将羞于作任何如此之坦认。接着提醒自己：非未来或过去压在你身上，而永远是当下——并且当下在你将其单独抽离、并盘诘自己的心念时会变得轻省。

sections.english: Is Panthea or Pergamus still sitting by the coffin of Verus? Or Chabrias or Diotimus by Hadrian's? Ridiculous! And if they were still sitting there, would the dead be aware? And if they were aware, would they be pleased? And if they were pleased, would that make their mourners immortal? Was it not their fate too to age in time and die? And when they died, what would those mourned do?
sections.chinese: 潘忒亚或佩尔伽穆斯还坐在维鲁斯之棺旁吗？或卡布里亚斯或狄奥提穆斯还在哈德良之棺旁吗？可笑之极！即便他们仍守坐彼处，死者能知觉吗？若能知觉，他们会高兴吗？若他们高兴，这能让哀悼者永生不死吗？哀悼者不也注定要随时日而老迈、终归死去吗？当他们死去，那些被哀悼者又该何如？

sections.english: If you have sharp sight, use it: but, as the poet says, add wise judgement.
sections.chinese: 若你有敏锐之眼力，使用它：但如诗人所言，更要加之明智之判断。

sections.english: In the constitution of the rational being I can see no virtue that counters justice: but I do see the counter to pleasure — self-control.
sections.chinese: 在理性存在者之构造中，我看不出有任何美德可与正义相抗衡：然我确实看见了对抗逸乐者——那便是自制。

sections.english: If you remove your judgement of anything that seems painful, you yourself stand quite immune to pain. 'What self?' Reason. 'But I am not just reason.' Granted. So let your reason cause itself no pain, and if some other part of you is in trouble, it can form its own judgement for itself.
sections.chinese: 若你将对任何看似痛苦之事物的评判移除，你自身便全然不受痛楚。哪一自我？理性。但我并非仅是理性。诚然。那便让你的理性不给自己制造痛楚，而若你某个其他部分有困扰，它自可为它本身做其判断。

sections.english: An obstacle to sense perception is harmful to animal nature. An obstacle to impulse is likewise harmful to animal nature. It follows that an obstacle to the mind is harmful to intelligent nature. Now apply all this to yourself. Does pain or pleasure affect you? Let the senses see to it. Is there an obstacle to your impulse? If your impulse was unconditional, then indeed an obstacle is harmful to your rational nature. But if you anticipated the obstacle, then your impulse is not yet harmed.
sections.chinese: 感觉知觉之障碍有害于动物本性。冲动之障碍同样有害于动物本性。由此推之：心灵之障碍有害于智性本质。如今将至理应用于你自己身上。痛苦或逸乐影响你了吗？让感官自己去管此事。有障碍阻了你的冲动吗？若你的冲动乃是无条件的，那么障碍确然有害于你之理性本性。但若你预先计及了障碍，则你的冲动尚未受伤害。

sections.english: I have no cause to hurt myself: I have never consciously hurt anyone else.
sections.chinese: 我没有伤害己身之由：我也从未有意伤害过任何他人。

sections.english: Joy varies from person to person. My joy is if I keep my directing mind pure, denying no human being or human circumstance, but looking on all things with kindly eyes, giving welcome or use to each as it deserves.
sections.chinese: 悦乐因人而异。我之悦乐，在于我保持主导之心灵纯净，不拒斥任何人或任何人事之境，而以善意之眼观看一切，赋予每者以其所应得之接纳或运用。

sections.english: Look, make yourself a gift of this present time. Those who are more inclined to pursue fame hereafter fail to reckon that the next generation will have people just like those they dislike now: and they too will die. What, anyway, is it to you if this is the echo in future voices and this the judgement they pass on you?
sections.chinese: 看，将此时光化为你给自己之厚礼。那些更热衷于追求身后之名的人，未能算及：下一代也将满是这样的人——正如如今他们所不喜的那些人一般无二：且他们也将死去。无论如何，若未来之回声中他们如此评断你，这于你又有何干？

sections.english: Nothing can happen to any human being outside the experience which is natural to humans — an ox too experiences nothing foreign to the nature of oxen, a vine nothing foreign to the nature of vines, a stone nothing outside the property of a stone. So if each thing experiences what is usual and natural for it, why should you take exception? Universal nature has not made you such as to find intolerable what is part of her own dispensation.
sections.chinese: 没有任何事会发生于任何人类身外之事——那些超出人类自然经验之外的事。一头牛也不会经历与牛之本性相隔阂的事，一藤蔓亦不经验与藤蔓本性无关的事，一石头亦不历其石固有属性之外的事。故若每物皆经历对其为常见而自然之事，你又为何要生气？宇宙自然未将你造成会发现其自身安排之一部分为不可忍受者。

sections.english: If your distress has some external cause, it is not the thing itself that troubles you, but your own judgement of it — and you can erase this immediately. If it is something in your own attitude that distresses you, no one stops you correcting your view. So too if you are distressed at not achieving some envisaged good, why not rather concentrate on the achievement rather than the distress?
sections.chinese: 若你之烦恼有某种外在原因，则非事物本身在困扰你，而是你于此事之判断——而你可以立即消除它。若困扰你得是你自身态度中之某种东西，那便无人阻止你纠正你的看法。若你于此焦虑则是困于未能达成某设想之善，那何不集中精力于达成而非烦恼？

sections.english: Remember that your directing mind becomes invincible when it withdraws into its own self-sufficiency, not doing anything it does not wish to do, even if its position is unreasonable. How much more, then, when the judgement it forms is reasoned and deliberate? That is why a mind free from passions is a fortress: there is no stronger place of retreat for a man, and anyone taking refuge there is then invincible.
sections.chinese: 当记：你的主导心灵退归自我之自足中、不做它不愿做之事时——即便其所处之境不合理——便已不可战胜。那么当它所下的判断乃是经推理兼审慎的，又该何其更不可战胜呢？这便是何以无激情之心灵乃是一座堡垒：世间无更牢固之退隐处所，凡藏身于此之人，此后便不可征服。

sections.english: Do not elaborate to yourself beyond what your initial impressions report. You have been told that so-and-so is maligning you. That is the report: you have not been told that you are harmed. I see that my little boy is ill. That is what I see: I do not see that he is in danger. So always stay like that, not adding from within to what you are told, and you will not be harmed.
sections.chinese: 勿在初次印象所报者之外再加油添醋。你听说某某在诋毁你。这是所报告之事：你并未听到你受了伤害。我见我小儿病了。此为我之所见：我未见他陷入危险。故恒常如此——不于所报之事外再添从内而生之内容——你便不会受伤害。

sections.english: A bitter cucumber? Throw it away. Brambles in the path? Go round them. That is all you need, without going on to ask, 'So why are these things in the world anyway?' That question would be laughable to a student of nature, just as any carpenter or cobbler would laugh at you if you objected to the shavings or offcuts from their work in their shops.
sections.chinese: 一只苦黄瓜？扔掉便是。路中有荆棘？绕开它们便是。这便是你需要做的全部，不必再追问「那么这些物事到底为何存于世间？」此一问在有识于自然之学的人看来，是可笑的——正如任何木匠或补鞋匠若听见你反感作坊中之木屑或废皮料，也会嗤笑你一般。

sections.english: Do not be dilatory in action, muddled in communication, or vague in thought. Don't let your mind settle into depression or elation. Allow some leisure in your life. They kill, they cut in pieces, they hunt with curses. What relevance has this to keeping your mind pure, sane, sober, just? As if a man were to walk up to a clear spring of sweet water and curse it — the spring will not stop bubbling up its fresh water.
sections.chinese: 勿于行动拖拉，勿于沟通含混，勿于思想模糊。勿令你的心灵陷入消沉或亢奋。允些许闲暇入你生命之中。他们杀戮，他们将人碎尸，他们以诅咒追猎——这与你持守心灵纯净、清明、清醒、正直又有何关涉？正如一人走到一甘泉清源前去咒骂它——泉源不会因此停止涌出其鲜活之水。

sections.english: Someone who does not know that there is an ordered universe does not know where he is. Someone who does not know the natural purpose of the universe does not know who he is or what the universe is. Someone who fails in any one of these ways could not tell the purpose of his own existence either. So what do you think of the man who runs from or courts the applause of a public who have no idea where they are or who they are?
sections.chinese: 人不识有一秩序井然之宇宙，便不知己身在何处。人不识宇宙之自然目的，便不知自己是谁，亦不知宇宙为何物。在任何一项上有所失缺的人，亦讲不出自己存在之目的。那么，你对一个要避开或是追求那全然不知身在何处、不知己为何人之大众掌声的人，又作何想法？

sections.english: Do you want the praise of a man who curses himself three times an hour? Do you want to please a man who can't please himself? Can a man please himself when he regrets almost everything he does?
sections.chinese: 你愿取一每小时内咒骂自己三次的人之赞赏吗？你想取悦一个不能取悦自己的人吗？一个人倘若几乎后悔自己所做的所有事，他能取悦自己吗？

sections.english: Don't now just take your breath from the surrounding air, but take your thought too from the mind which embraces all things. The power of mind spreads everywhere and permeates no less than the air: it is there for all who want to absorb it, just like the air for those who can draw breath.
sections.chinese: 不要仅从周遭空气吸取你的呼吸，也从那怀抱万物的心智中吸取你的思想。心智之力弥漫遍地，渗透无所不在，不下于空气：它摆在那里为所有愿吸纳它的人备用——正如空气为能呼吸者备用一般。

sections.english: Wickedness overall does no harm to the universe. Individual wickedness does no harm to the recipient: it is only harmful to the perpetrator, and he has the option to be rid of it just as soon as he himself decides.
sections.chinese: 总体而言，邪恶于宇宙并无害。个体之邪恶于承受者并无害：它仅有害于那行恶者，而他一俟自己决定，便可转身弃去此恶。

sections.english: To my determining will my neighbour's will is as indifferent as his breath and his body. Sure, we are born above all for the sake of each other: nevertheless the directing mind of each of us has its own sovereignty. Otherwise my neighbour's wickedness would be my own harm: and this was not god's intention, that my misfortune could depend on someone else.
sections.chinese: 于我的决择之意志来说，邻人之意志正如其呼吸、身体一般，于我漠不相干。固然，吾辈天生最要紧的是为了彼此之缘故；然而吾辈各自之主导心灵皆有自身之主权。否则，邻人之邪恶便会成为我之伤害：而神意并非如此——我的厄运竟要系于他人之身。

sections.english: The sun appears to pour itself down, and indeed its light pours in all directions, but the stream does not run out. This pouring is linear extension: that is why its beams are called rays, because they radiate in extended lines. You can see what a ray is if you observe the sun's light entering a dark room through a narrow chink: it travels in a straight line and strikes, so to speak, any solid body which blocks its passage through the air beyond. There the light stops, without slipping off or falling. Now the flow of your thoughts should be like that: not pouring out, but extended. Their pressure on any obstacles it meets should be firm and steady: no violence or collapsing impact.
sections.chinese: 太阳似向下倾泻己身，而实则是其光芒在向一切方向流溢，然其流却不枯竭。此一流溢乃是直线延伸：故其光束被称为射线，因它们以延伸之线而辐射。你若观察太阳之光经一窄隙渗入幽暗之室中，便可见何为一道射线：它沿直线行进，撞击在（可以如是说）任何挡在超出空气路径之外的固形物体之上。光便停在彼处，不滑落、不坍坠。你的思想之流动亦当如此：不漫溢，而是延伸而前进。对于其所遇障碍，其挤压力应坚定而平顺：无暴戾或垮塌之冲击。

sections.english: He who fears death fears either unconsciousness or another sort of consciousness. Now if you will no longer be conscious you will not be conscious either of anything bad. If you are to take on a different consciousness, you will be a different being and life will not cease.
sections.chinese: 凡畏惧死亡者，其所畏者要么是无知觉，要么是别一种知觉。然若你将不再有知觉，你便也不会知觉任何坏事了。若你将承接一种不同之知觉，你便将是一个不同之存在，而生命亦不会终结。

sections.english: Men are born for the sake of each other. So either teach or tolerate.
sections.chinese: 人皆彼此而生。故，要么教诲，要么容耐。

sections.english: An arrow flies in one way, the mind in another. Yet even when it is keeping on the alert or circling round an inquiry, the mind moves no less directly, and straight to its target.
sections.chinese: 箭矢以某一方式飞行，心灵则以另一种方式。然即便当它保持警觉或围绕一探究盘旋之刻，心灵之移动仍是直线而向标的，一如其直接飞行时一般无误。

sections.english: Enter into the directing mind of everyone, and let anyone else enter your own.
sections.chinese: 进入每人主导之心灵，亦容许别人进入你自己的。
